classification.fixedClientDefectsVerified: This report's direct evidence is the final auto3 sequential scenario: signed-device encryption, all six remote routes for 60 seconds, leave/rejoin, first-user departure/rejoin and device transfer passed with no collected console errors. Deterministic client regression outcomes are recorded separately by the main agent. This real-path success does not imply that every SFU matrix passes.
classification.explicitProviderNonAllocation: HTTP 200 per-track not_found_track_error or temporarily_unavailable_error with empty MID is an explicit non-allocation, not an unknown allocated track. Bounded retries preserve successful tracks.
classification.unknownResult: 502 or aborted upstream operations do not prove non-allocation. A new-session 502 without a returned session ID fails safely; no blind reuse/reallocation is claimed.
classification.remainingClientRecoveryBoundary: Some no-console-error failures lack required routes or empty-room readiness. Their stage traces identify slow transport/negotiation but do not by themselves prove a client bug or purely provider failure.
classification.latencyCausality: Endpoint offsets and localhost backend request durations are measured. The backend durations include authentication, queueing, event-loop load and upstream work. Parallel full UI tests mean CPU/network normality was not established; no single provider-only cause is inferred.
classification.remainingAcceptance: Both complete 10 concurrent + 10 rotation matrices, strict P95 gates, exclusive normal-network timing, physical audio devices and cross-network production acceptance remain incomplete.
classification.persistedCandidateSnapshotBoundary: The initial 3-user relay sustained-audio endpoint snapshot omits a selected pair on some routes although the polling predicate required a real relay. Its report flags this omission; it is not repaired from configuration. Initial 5-user relay and final 3/5-user auto sustained snapshots retain selected pairs for every route.
